messages:
marco: FYI I started a thread because I bumped into a regression after the kernel-selector change rolled last night. batch wait p95 is up ~110ms in prod and token-level tail latency increased. attaching quick notes below.

perf-alert-bot: [ALERT] queue_wait_p95=220ms for pool=redwood-prod-us-west-2 (rate window=5m)

marta: ouch. any obvious correlation with KV cache?

marco: KV cache hit rate dipped from 0.89 -> 0.71 around the same time. profiler snapshot shows more kernel-switch paths being taken per request. suspect selector now prefers packed kernels that increase bundle latency on small batches.

cheng: can you paste the pprof or the metric queries you used?

marco: sure. quick grafana queries I ran: \n```\n// batch size histogram (5m)\nhistogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batcher_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))\n// queue wait p95\nquantile_over_time(0.95, queue_wait_seconds[5m])\n// per-token kernel handoff count\nsum(rate(kernel_handoffs_total[5m])) by (kernel, pool)\n```\n
marco: snapshots: p50 queue_wait=18ms, p95=220ms, batch_size p50=3, p95=16. token latency p95 increased by +26ms. KVcache_miss_rate spiked to ~0.29.

sam: is the selector scoring function now weighting model_size_match higher than latency_estimate? I remember that change in PR #4123.

marta: yes PR had a tweak — weigh_model_alignment=0.65 -> 0.8. that should prefer kernels with better packed throughput. might be hurting small-batch tails.

cheng: if we can reproduce in staging, we can flip the weight back and run canary. can someone trigger a synthetic load that mimics small chat sessions?

ops: I can run the load generator on staging (p3a-8x). what exact distribution do you want?

marco: mimic production small-session mix: 70% requests <= 64 tokens, 25% 65-512, 5% >512. ramp 200rps for 5m then 1k rps for 10m. enable random KV cache TTL jitter to surface misses.

tori: uploaded a pprof from one node to /tmp/profiles/1745629012.pprof and a flamegraph to the perf bucket (s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/). link: https://perf.redwood/s/1745629012

sam: looking at the flamegraph — lots of time in kernel_pack_and_dispatch when batch_size<8. the packed kernel path does extra copy/serialize steps that are amortized poorly on tiny batches.

marta: two options: 1) revert the weight change in kernel selector (quick) 2) make selector use an estimated batch-size-aware penalty term so it prefers latency-optimized kernels when expected_batch_size < threshold.

cheng: preference: do both. revert to stabilize prod, then land the smarter heuristic with a canary. i can prototype the expected_batch_size estimator — use recent 30s batch size hist distribution per pool.

ops: rolling revert to canary pool now (redwood-prod-canary). will watch queue_wait and kvcache metrics.

perf-alert-bot: [INFO] deploy started: kernel-selector-revert by ops at 1745629120

marco: thanks. also let's add a quick dashboard card showing "selector chosen kernel vs estimated_batch_size" and surface when kvcache_miss_rate > 0.2. that will help correlate in future.

tori: added a draft panel in dashboards/runtime/perf - panel id 112 (needs perms). shows a stacked count of kernel_choice by estimated_batch_size bucket.

sam: short-term mitigation idea: bump continuous-batching max_wait_ms from 10ms -> 20ms for small pools to increase batch sizes slightly. could reduce kernel_switch churn. downside: latency floor might increase for p50.

marta: log that playbook in runbook: "if packed-kernel tail regresses -> revert selector weight, increase max_wait_ms temporarily, canary smarter heuristic". I'll update the runbook after this thread.

ops: canary revert is in, canary queue_wait p95 dropped from 210ms -> 45ms within 2 mins. monitoring across main pool now.

marco: excellent. creating a perf-task: track regression post-mitigation in the 24h window, add an integration test that runs batcher under small-batch workload to catch selector regressions. tagging @cheng and @sam.

cheng: will PR estimator and unit tests today.

sam: i'll open the integration test and add the dashboard alarm threshold for selector_kernel_mismatch.

perf-alert-bot: [RESOLVED] queue_wait_p95 back to normal for pool=redwood-prod-us-west-2 (value=48ms)

marta: thanks everyone. final note: let's keep an eye on KV cache TTL churn — I suspect a compaction window in the cache coincided with the deploy which amplified misses. ops can you confirm compaction schedule?

ops: compaction window was at 17:40 UTC which aligns with this. noting in the incident log.

marco: closing the thread for now; will reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
